`useLayoutEffect` runs synchronously after the DOM updates but before the browser paints, so use it when you need to measure layout (sizes, positions) and update state before the user sees a frame, like positioning a tooltip, to avoid a flicker. `useEffect` runs after paint and is right for almost everything else, such as fetching, subscriptions and logging. In server-rendered code `useLayoutEffect` doesn't run on the server, so it can warn in SSR. Action: no code change needed; point me to a specific component if you want me to look at one.

They're different. HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only reuses a TCP connection for sequential requests, so each connection still has one request in flight at a time and browsers open several connections per host to compensate. HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent request/response streams over a single connection, interleaving frames, so there's no HTTP-level head-of-line blocking (TCP-level blocking remains, which HTTP/3 addresses). Action: none.

A Deployment treats pods as interchangeable and stateless, so they get random names and share (or have no) storage. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable name and network identity (pod-0, pod-1, via a headless Service), its own persistent volume from `volumeClaimTemplates`, and ordered startup, scaling and rollout. Pick it for databases, brokers and clustered systems that need stable identity or per-replica disks. Action: none.
